title: Ginseng tincture for low energy
subtitle: A long-course tincture of Panax ginseng root for sustained tiredness and depletion
excerpt: Ginseng tincture is a 1:5 extract of dried Panax ginseng root in 40% spirit, taken in small doses over 6 to 8 weeks. Traditionally prepared in the Chinese and Korean herbal traditions for sustained low energy, depletion, and difficulty recovering from illness or stress. A 100 ml bottle holds about 20 doses and keeps two years in a dark cupboard.
sourceNotes: WHO monographs on selected medicinal plants vol. 1 (1999), Radix Ginseng, open access. EMA HMPC Community herbal monograph on Panax ginseng C.A. Meyer, radix (2014, EMA/HMPC/321232/2012), open access. Felter & Lloyd, King's American Dispensatory (1898), ginseng entry.

recipe.yieldDescription: 100 ml herbal extract (approx. 20 doses at 5 ml)
recipe.makeAheadNotes: steep for 4 to 6 weeks before straining. The finished herbal extract keeps 2 years in a sealed dark glass bottle.

projectSchedule.title: Start maceration
projectSchedule.body: Weigh out 20 g of dried ginseng root. Place in a clean jar. Pour over 100 ml of 40% vodka or gin. Seal tightly and label with the date.

projectSchedule.title: Check and stir
projectSchedule.body: Open the jar and check that the liquid still covers the root. If the root has absorbed liquid and is exposed, top up with a little more spirit. The liquid should be turning amber. Reseal.

projectSchedule.title: Taste
projectSchedule.body: Take a small amount on a spoon and taste. Ginseng should taste bitter, slightly sweet, and earthy. If the flavour is still mild, macerate a further two weeks.

projectSchedule.title: Strain and bottle
projectSchedule.body: Strain the tincture through muslin into a dark glass bottle, pressing the root to extract as much liquid as possible. Label with the herb, spirit percentage, and date. Store in a cool dark cupboard.

content.text: Ginseng herbal extract is a dark amber extract of dried Panax ginseng root macerating in 40% spirit for 4 to 6 weeks, strained and bottled. A long-course preparation traditionally taken in small daily doses for sustained low energy, depletion, and difficulty recovering after illness or a period of high demand. The taste is bitter, slightly sweet, and earthy. A 100 ml bottle at 1:5 provides about 20 doses at 5 ml, a 4 to 5 week course at the standard dose, and keeps two years in a cool dark cupboard.

attrs.title: Precautions
attrs.body: Not medical advice. Consult a qualified herbalist or doctor before use. Full precautions are in the 'When not to use' section.

items.prepNote: dried root, sliced or coarsely ground
plain 40% ABV vodka or gin, the spirit must be at least 40% to preserve the herbal extract

content.text: Weigh out 20 g of dried ginseng root. Place in a clean, dry steeping jar with a tight-fitting lid.
Pour 100 ml of 40% spirit over the root. The root should be covered by the liquid. Seal tightly and label with the herb name and the date.
Store in a cool dark cupboard for 4 to 6 weeks, shaking the jar every few days. At week two, check that the root is still submerged, top up with a little more spirit if it has been absorbed.

When the steeping period is complete, strain through doubled muslin into a dark glass bottle. Press or squeeze the root firmly to extract as much liquid as possible. Seal, label, and store in a cool dark cupboard.

3 to 5 ml in a small glass of water, taken once in the morning. Ginseng is a stimulating tonic and is best not taken in the evening. Take for 6 to 8 weeks, then take a 2 to 4 week break before deciding whether to continue. If you notice sleep disruption, palpitations, or headaches, reduce the dose or stop.
Keep in a sealed dark glass bottle in a cool dark cupboard. Keeps for two years from the date of straining.
When not to use this remedy

Do not use in pregnancy, with anticoagulant medication, or if you have uncontrolled high blood pressure. See a doctor if fatigue is severe, came on suddenly, or comes with unexplained weight loss, night sweats, or does not improve with rest.
